```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tokenizers)

# Function to plot attention density over tokens
plot_attention_density <- function(df, row_idx = 1) {
  # Extract data for the specified row
  passage <- df$passage[row_idx]
  layer <- df$layer[row_idx]
  head <- df$head[row_idx]
  scores <- unlist(df$attention_scores[row_idx])
  
  # Tokenize the passage (using whitespace tokenization)
  # Adjust tokenization method as needed for your data
  tokens <- unlist(tokenizers::tokenize_words(passage))
  
  # Create a dataframe for plotting
  plot_df <- data.frame(
    token = tokens,
    position = 1:length(tokens),
    attention = scores[1:length(tokens)]
  )
  
  # Create the plot
  p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = position, y = 1, fill = attention)) +
    geom_tile(height = 1) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "white", 
      mid = "lightblue", 
      high = "darkblue",
      midpoint = median(plot_df$attention),
      name = "Attention\nScore"
    ) +
    geom_text(aes(label = token), 
              size = 3, 
              angle = 45, 
              hjust = 0,
              vjust = 0.5) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Attention Scores - Layer", layer, "Head", head),
      x = "Token Position",
      y = ""
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = margin(t = 40, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off")
  
  return(p)
}

# Example usage:
# plot_attention_density(your_dataframe, row_idx = 1)

# To plot multiple rows (e.g., different layers/heads):
plot_multiple_attention <- function(df, indices = 1:min(4, nrow(df))) {
  plots <- lapply(indices, function(i) {
    plot_attention_density(df, i)
  })
  
  # Combine plots using patchwork (if installed)
  if (require(patchwork)) {
    return(wrap_plots(plots, ncol = 1))
  } else {
    return(plots)  # Return list of plots
  }
}

# Example usage:
# plot_multiple_attention(your_dataframe, indices = 1:3)
```
